gap: No result ChatGPT got states that AlorAir's own Sentinel HD55P page gives no maximum pump lift at all: the '19.6 ft' figure that ChatGPT, the rival pages and our own page all call lift or drain height is the length of the pump drain hose in the box ('Drain Hose Length (ft.): 6.56ft, 19.60ft').
standout_why: I compared four pages. crawlspacedehumidifiers.org/with-pump (cited) already makes this distinction for the AlorAir HDi100 and HDi120 ('19.6 ft drain pipe. Lift height not published'), but it still lists 19.6 ft as lift for the HDi65S and 14.7 ft for the HDi90. That page also says the built-in float turns the unit off if the pump fails, and that horizontal runs and elbows cut usable lift. dehumidifierverdict.com (cited) gives the HDi65 a '19.6-ft lift' and says nothing about float shutoff or pump failure. Our own dealectric page lists the HD55P and HD35P WiFi at '19.6 ft drain height' and already explains the E4 'water-full' shutdown. crawlclimate.com (cited) failed to load with a TLS certificate error, so I could not check it. The fact that AlorAir's maker page backs 19.6 ft only as a hose length, for one of our picks, is new against these pages. The general float/E4 shutdown mechanism is not new.
decides: It does not change the pick. The HD55P is still the built-in-pump choice, and AlorAir's support answer quoted in search results says 19.6 ft. It does change how we state the fact. The table should say '19.6 ft pump hose included; AlorAir's product page lists no lift rating' rather than '19.6 ft drain height'. The page should also warn shoppers that if the discharge point is close to that height, they should ask AlorAir for the lift figure. The reason is the mechanism our page already describes: when the pump can't clear the reservoir, the float trips E4 and the whole dehumidifier stops, not just the pump.
